result.reviewScopeSummary: Follow-up verification focused on the prior stale-write blocker across the touched smooth-turn persistence path, the new regression test, the story gate, a reopen persistence check, and an isolated-writer reproduction using the current `persistSmoothTurnState` path.

priorFindingStatuses.rationale:
The quick fix closes the same-process stale-snapshot case by re-reading thread state before patching a single turn, and the new regression at `tests/thread/smooth-turn-service.test.ts:610-714` passes. But the runtime still relies on process-local `withSerializedThreadOperation` (`src/context-steward/services/thread-service.ts:41-63`) plus whole-file `writeTurns` (`src/context-steward/store/file-thread-store.ts:338-366`) instead of the design’s thread-scoped mutation lease (`docs/spec-build/epics/03-deterministic-band-and-projection-mechanics/tech-design.md:115`, `docs/spec-build/epics/03-deterministic-band-and-projection-mechanics/tech-design-thread.md:121`, `docs/spec-build/epics/03-deterministic-band-and-projection-mechanics/tech-design-thread.md:291-303`). A two-child-process reproduction against the current `persistSmoothTurnState` path still lost one turn’s smooth record, ending with `[{"turnId":"turn-a","generatedAt":"2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z","smoothText":"[user]
Prompt 1

[assistant]
Response 1"},{"turnId":"turn-b"}]`.

openFindings.title: Whole-snapshot turn writes can erase previously generated smooth state
openFindings.evidence:
`persistSmoothTurnState` and `ensureSmoothTurn` now re-open thread state before writing, but they still serialize only through the in-process queue in `withSerializedThreadOperation` (`src/context-steward/services/thread-service.ts:41-63`) and still commit via whole-file `writeTurns` (`src/context-steward/store/file-thread-store.ts:338-366`). The design still calls for a thread-scoped mutation coordinator with expected-revision enforcement for async-thread writes (`docs/spec-build/epics/03-deterministic-band-and-projection-mechanics/tech-design.md:115`, `docs/spec-build/epics/03-deterministic-band-and-projection-mechanics/tech-design-thread.md:121`, `docs/spec-build/epics/03-deterministic-band-and-projection-mechanics/tech-design-thread.md:291-303`). A live two-child-process reproduction using the current `persistSmoothTurnState` path left one closed turn unsmoothed: `[{"turnId":"turn-a","generatedAt":"2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z","smoothText":"[user]
Prompt 1

[assistant]
Response 1"},{"turnId":"turn-b"}]`. That means closed turns can still lose deterministic smooth state when writes come from isolated writers.

productionPathFindings: The touched smooth-turn runtime path still depends on a process-local serializer instead of a real thread-scoped mutation lease, so isolated writers can still race and drop one turn’s persisted smooth artifact.
additionalObservations: The quick fix did resolve the original same-process stale-snapshot case: the new regression test at `tests/thread/smooth-turn-service.test.ts:610-714` passed, and all 8 mapped Story 1 TCs plus the noise-section decided test remained green.
A manual reopen check still confirmed the happy path persists smooth state on Turn records across a fresh `FileThreadStore` instance.
No fake adapter, placeholder branch, or mock-only production path was introduced in the touched smooth-turn formatter/service code.
